title: Five Moons in One Picture: Luna Meets Jupiter
summary: A photographer captured Earth's Moon passing in front of Jupiter, with four of Jupiter's moons visible alongside it. The image shows five moons in a single frame.

sections.heading: Counting Five Moons
sections.body: How many moons can you spot in this image? The best answer is five: four circling Jupiter and Luna, which is Earth's Moon. The picture was possible because Earth's Moon moved directly in front of Jupiter last week.

sections.heading: How the Image Was Made
sections.body: The featured image is a series of exposures taken near the time of alignment from Westchester, New York, USA. The sunlit crescent of Earth's Moon, at lower left, is overexposed, meaning it appears extra bright. The Moon's night side, at upper right, glows faintly from Earthshine, which is sunlight reflected off Earth onto the Moon.

sections.heading: Jupiter's Galilean Moons
sections.body: Lined up nearly vertically above our Moon, from bottom to top, are Jupiter's bright Galilean satellites: Ganymede, Io, Callisto, and Europa. Callisto, Ganymede, and Io are larger than Earth's Moon, while Europa is only slightly smaller.

sections.heading: Juno at Jupiter
sections.body: NASA's robotic spacecraft Juno is currently orbiting Jupiter. It has made close passes near three of these moons. The image is credited to Chirag Upreti.
